data.narrative:
CubeSpace is a growth-stage company in Space & Aerospace, founded by Mike-Alec Kearney, Willem Jordaan, and Jako Gerber. The valuation exercise draws on a sector universe of 13 peers: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Standard peer-median triangulation is not applicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints within CubeSpace's narrow stage and valuation band. Of 14 same-sector peers identified, none meet simultaneous criteria for stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, and valuation-tier similarity—a minimum threshold of 3 datapoints was not achieved. Public-comp anchoring via sector P/S multiples is also not feasible; the Space & Aerospace median trades at 25.3x revenue across the 6 public tickers, but CubeSpace's revenue figure is not on file, precluding application of this method.

Without disclosed revenue or a sufficiently dense peer set at equivalent growth and maturity levels, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range. Key uncertainties include CubeSpace's current revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and technical/regulatory milestones relative to the private peer cohort. A credible valuation would require either: revenue disclosure to anchor public-comp methods, or identification of at least three private comparables with matching stage and financial transparency.
